summary.tldr: Changes Employment Insurance rules for pregnancy, parental and critically ill adult care benefits, including a 26-week limit for critically ill adult care.
what_it_does: Exempts benefits paid because of pregnancy, or because a claimant is caring for a newborn or an adopted child, from the combined weeks of benefits rule.
Extends the benefit period for claimants who receive pregnancy or parental benefits.
Raises the maximum weeks of benefits for caring for or supporting a critically ill adult from 15 to 26, for Employment Insurance claimants and self-employed claimants.
Allows two claimants caring for the same critically ill adult to divide up to 26 weeks of benefits between them, under the Employment Insurance and self-employed rules.
Repeals subsection 12(7) and Schedule IV of the Employment Insurance Act.
who_it_affects: People caring for a critically ill adult
summary.background: The bill amends the Employment Insurance Act. It changes rules for combining weeks of benefits and for benefit periods linked to pregnancy, parental leave and care for critically ill adults.
